frequency_question: How often do US presidents follow through on announced major tariff threats against key allies/partners within the stated timeframe?
membership_rule: Includes announced broad tariff rates on specific allied partner nations where executive authority was invoked; excludes purely multilateral WTO disputes or generalized non-specific legislative actions.
provenance_note: 6 cases named, 7 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.2x)
coverage_note: 6 named; believed roughly 7 in total for major unilateral tariff threats enacted by executive action.
known_gaps: Excludes minor or threatened-only tariff measures that were purely rhetorical leverage without formal administrative action initiated.
skeleton: Key executive tariff announcements since 1970 that reached implementation stage vs. those rescinded prior to deadline.
multiplier: 6 hits out of 7 total major unilateral tariff announcements where initial threat was carried to implementation or initial execution phase (1 case modified later, counted as hit for initial implementation).
validity_reason: Executive authority under trade statutes remains stable across administrations, governed by long-standing statutory frameworks.
